Search Query: I’m starting a pretty intense master’s program next semester and I’ll probably be living 30–40 minutes from campus because rent near school is rough. Should I prioritize paying more to live closer to campus, or can I make a commuter setup work? What should I look for in study spaces and local amenities so I’m not wasting time, money, or focus every week?
Evidence nuggets:
- n0 -- Long commute (>1 hr) cuts focus, sleep, study time -- vital

- n2 -- Campus library offers quiet, focused environment, free tech -- vital
- n3 -- Public libraries offer free tech, quiet spaces, printing, tutoring -- vital
- n4 -- Outdoor study reduces screen fatigue, boosts concentration, good weather needed -- okay
- n5 -- Coffee shop ambient noise 50‑70 dB can improve focus -- vital
- n6 -- Coffee shop chairs poor ergonomics; opt for comfortable seating -- vital
- n7 -- Coworking day pass $20‑$40 gives flexible workspace, occasional private rooms -- vital
- n8 -- Check campus transport free shuttle or discounted fares -- vital
- n9 -- Good Wi‑Fi and power outlets crucial: cafés unreliable -- vital
- n10 -- Tidy space promotes persistence, reduces frustration -- vital
- n11 -- Natural light reduces fatigue, boosts alertness -- vital
- n12 -- Time of day aligns with personal alertness schedule -- vital
- n13 -- Consider bike or foot commute for health and flexibility -- vital
- n14 -- Use commuting time for reading or note review -- vital
- n15 -- Booking library seats in advance ensures study spot -- vital
- n16 -- Guard against high café prices adding to budget -- vital
- n17 -- Verify parking fees near campus; create cost plan -- vital
- n18 -- Outdoor spaces benefit mental health, lower stress -- okay
- n19 -- Study space with optimal ambient noise helps some -- vital

Return ONLY the JSON object. Do not use Markdown fences and do not explain.

</file>
